correctness.rationale: The conditional hypergeometric expected payoff gap is affine in X and is established from exact factorial-moment identities. The one-step transition ratio equals exp(-w Δ_X), giving the closed fixation denominator. The full four-way parameter classification follows from Jensen, strict convexity of the exponential sum, its exact first derivative at zero and sign of the endpoint prefixes. In strict-reversal windows, the population-size asymptotic follows from compact-uniform Riemann-sum convergence and the unique positive integral crossing. A standard-library independent calculation checked 1777 exact-payoff, recurrence and illustrative asymptotic assertions; none of the infinite assertions is inferred solely from finite computation.

originality.rationale: The underlying public-goods game, its general fixation formula, affine payoff structure and weak-selection condition appear in Hauert and McAvoy (2024) and are not claimed as original. The compared primary text does not provide the all-strength strict selection-neutrality reversal classification, unique crossing/maximum, or the explicit 1/N critical-strength law. Hindersin et al. (2019) provide generic fixation theory, not the nonlinear-game parameter windows; Wu et al. (2013) compare the relative fixation ordering, a mathematically different property. Related searched published findings concern pairwise assortativity, not this exact multiperson absorption problem. More general prior convex-exponential-sum or fixation results remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: Publication-priority checking is not exhaustive; general exponential-polynomial sign or evolutionary fixation results could subsume aspects of the classification.
The source uses a general finite-population model and provides the starting fixation identity; originality applies to further analytical implications, not that starting identity.
Independent review of the analytical derivation and historical novelty has not been performed.

value.rationale: The exact unique finite threshold answers a substantive, model-specific interpretation question omitted by weak-selection theory: cooperation may remain favored over defection while losing neutral fixation advantage as selection grows. It gives complete parameter windows for synergy and discounting, a unique optimal intensity, rigorous finite examples and a well-defined inverse-population scale. These are motivated changes in qualitative fixation behavior across strengths and population sizes, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice or a restatement of known first-order coefficients.
